summary: The base JIT implementation reproduced the reported source-level ABI mismatch: it resolved cudaMemcpyBatchAsync from the loaded runtime with dlsym but selected the 8- versus 9-argument function type from compile-time CUDA_VERSION. The correction now queries the loaded CUDA runtime and dispatches through the matching CUDA 12.8 or CUDA 13 signature, mirroring the existing AOT implementation. A host C++ regression compiled with CUDA_VERSION=12080 independently exercised both runtime boundaries (12999 and 13000).

tests.what_was_measured: A C++ harness compiled with the CUDA 12.8 macro dispatched a simulated CUDA 13 runtime to the 8-argument ABI and a pre-13 runtime to the 9-argument ABI, including the failIdx sentinel. 1 passed.
Existing HiCache host-pool and staged write-back dispatch behavior. 16 passed, 1 skipped.
Real JIT page-first staged MHA and MLA device-host round trips on the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 GPU, with independent tensor equality checks across 12 cases.

gpu_execution.evidence: The 12-case page-first staged write-back suite ran on AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 under torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-ea49c7d64e51/test-artifacts/gfx950-staged-write-back.txt. This validates only the unaffected ROCm JIT path, not CUDA ABI selection.

remaining_limitations: The assigned machine has ROCm 7.2 and one gfx950 GPU, not CUDA 12.8 headers plus a CUDA 13 libcudart. The original SIGSEGV, full 27B AWQ model, TP2 serving path, NVIDIA ISA, and real mixed-toolchain CUDA execution could not be reproduced here.
The new ABI regression uses typed simulated entry points in a native C++ harness. It verifies the exact argument-count boundary without invoking NVIDIA libcudart.
No model weights or multi-node workload were used.
